rules.description: Minimum 15 interviews for adequate qualitative saturation
JTBD school must be explicitly chosen (switch or odi, not both)
CJM TO BE must be labeled as hypothesis
LTV/CAC > 10 is suspicious at early stage
Minimum 2 prototype iterations required
LTV must be cohort-based
CAC must be fully-loaded
Minimum 5 users for usability testing (qualitative discovery)
Minimum 2 test iterations
VSM TO BE must be labeled as projection
Pilot must be conducted for L/XL tiers
Minimum 100 survey respondents for quantitative validation
A standardized usability instrument (SUS, target >68, or an ISO 9241-11 effectiveness/efficiency/satisfaction scaffold) must be used in Test — ad-hoc custom thresholds alone are insufficient

Pricing & conversion assumptions feeding unit economics must be empirically grounded (willingness-to-pay interview questions, Van Westendorp PSM, Gabor-Granger, conjoint, or a live A/B price test) or explicitly labeled as UNVALIDATED expert estimates — stated intent ('I would pay X') is not a validated price

Per-segment economics (ARPU, CAC, COGS) must use a matching segment numerator AND denominator — never divide blended multi-segment revenue by a single-segment user count; per-channel viability must not be masked by a favorable blend

Every headline ratio (ROI, payback, LTV/CAC) must be reproducible from disclosed inputs, and the same metric must reconcile across sections (channel CAC vs blended CAC) — a single source of truth, no undisclosed formulas

Load-bearing financial inputs sourced from outside the project (a teammate's workstream, an external benchmark) must be labeled borrowed-and-unvalidated AND carry a sensitivity analysis (at what input value does the model stop converging?)

A headline NPV/DCF/SOM/unit-economics figure built on un-piloted inputs must be labeled a projection and carry scenario/sensitivity analysis; TAM/SAM/SOM must disclose top-down vs bottom-up method and coefficient sources; SOM must reconcile with the bottom-up operational/financial forecast in the same model (flag order-of-magnitude divergence) and de-duplicate audience overlap when aggregating across platforms; a conversion-rate pilot needs enough conversion EVENTS (~5-10+), not just sessions, before its CR seeds unit economics

Team-deliverable scoping integrity: in a multi-author product, every load-bearing input inherited from a co-author (interview counts, personas, CJM, prototype, pricing, unit economics) must be labeled team-sourced and the author's own validated contribution delimited; a phase whose execution is delegated to a teammate is neither passed nor failed by THIS author — mark it DELEGATED-UNVERIFIED and do not count it toward a 'validated value proposition' claim (extends DT-017 beyond financials to all inherited empirical evidence)

Sample-segment alignment & selection bias (independent of the N thresholds in DT-001/DT-012): flag when the empirical sample composition (segment / company-size / recruitment channel) does not match the declared target ICP, or the frame is non-random/self-selected/captive (loyal base, professional community), or a representativeness/selection-bias caveat stated in methods is not propagated into the final conclusions

Sensitive-data compliance feasibility: products transmitting/storing PII, financial, health-adjacent, or otherwise regulated data must include a legal/regulatory feasibility analysis integrated into the DFV Viability axis (not merely a risk-register line); if a compliance prerequisite (data-localization, on-premise, certification) gates a target segment, it must be sequenced at market entry, not deferred to a later scale phase

Evidence-to-solution traceability: each load-bearing architecture/NFR/MVP-feature-priority decision must cite the specific empirical pain (interview/CJM/analytics/JTBD) it serves; an asserted 'decisions are linked to pains' claim without a concrete traced example, or a MoSCoW/RICE tier with no stated decider + backing evidence, is flagged as an untraced solution bolt-on (distinct from DFV-scoring, which scores clusters but does not require per-decision citation)

Threshold value justification & pre-registration integrity: a validation/confirmation threshold (HADI metric target OR a qualitative/survey confirmation cutoff) must be justified by a benchmark, baseline measurement, or recognized qualitative standard (theoretical saturation, inter-rater agreement) — pre-defining a number is necessary but not sufficient; additionally flag goalpost-moving (a hypothesis with a stated numeric pass-bar declared 'confirmed' on substitute/indirect evidence after the bar was missed). Distinct from the 'HADI without pre-defined metrics' anti-pattern, which only catches an absent threshold
